                     </ns0:note> chief house a prince, throughout all the tribes of Israel, and each one <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> an head of the house of <ns0:hi>their</ns0:hi> fathers among the thousands of Israel.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="15">15 ¶ And they came unto the children of Reuben, and to the children of Gad, and to the half tribe of Manasseh, unto the land of Gilead, and they spake with them, saying,</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="16">16 Thus saith the whole congregation of the Lord <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Who do and are resolved to cleave unto that God from whom you have revolted, and who speak this to you in the name of the Lord.</ns0:note>, What trespass <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> this <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">How heinous a crime is this!</ns0:note>, that ye have com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mitted against the God of Israel, to turn away this day <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> so soon after God hath obliged you by such wonderful favours, and when God is now conducting you home to reap the fruits of all your pains and hazards.</ns0:note> from following the LORD, in that ye have builded you an altar, that ye might rebel <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">With a design to revolt from, and rebel against God, and against his express command of worshipping him at one onely Altar, <ns0:hi>Exo. l.</ns0:hi> 20. 24. <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 17. 8, 9. <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 12. 5, 11, 13.</ns0:note> this day against the LORD?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="17">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:188" />17 Is the iniquity <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">Numb. 25. 4.</ns0:note> of Peor <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Of our worshipping of <ns0:hi>Baal-Peor, Numb.</ns0:hi> 25.</ns0:note> too little for us, from which we are not cleansed until this day <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">For though God had pardoned it, as to the National Punishment of it, <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 25. 11. Yet they were not yet thorowly pur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ged from it; partly because the shame and blot of that filthy and odious practise was not yet wiped of: and partly, because some of that corrupt leaven still remained among them, and though smothered for a time, yet was ready to break forth upon all occasions. See <ns0:hi>Ios.</ns0:hi> 24. 23. And God also took no<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tice of these Idolatrous inclinations in particular persons, and found out ways to punish them one time or other.</ns0:note> (although there was a plague in the congregation of the LORD)</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="18">18 But that ye must turn away this day from following the LORD? and it will be, <ns0:hi>seeing</ns0:hi> ye re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bel to day against the LORD, that to morrow <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Suddenly, as that word is oft used, as <ns0:hi>Matt.</ns0:hi> 6. 30. 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 15. 32.</ns0:note> he will be wroth with the whole congregation of Israel <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">With you for doing so, and with us for suffering, or not punishing it.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="19">19 Notwithstanding, if the land of your possessi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on <ns0:hi>be</ns0:hi> unclean <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">If you apprehend it to be so for want of the Taberna<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cle and Altar there; as the following words imply: if you now repent of your former choice in preferring the world<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly commodities of that Country before the advantage of Gods presence and favour, and more frequent opportunities of his Service.</ns0:note>, <ns0:hi>then</ns0:hi> pass ye over unto the land of the possession of the LORD, wherein the LORD's tabernacle dwelleth, and take possession among us <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">We will readily resign part of our possessi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ons to you for the prevention of this sin and mischief, wherein they shew great zeal for Gods honour, and great pity and charity to their Brethren.</ns0:note>: but rebel not against the LORD, nor rebel against us, in building you an altar, beside the altar of the LORD our God.<ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">For all the tribes were united in one Body Politick, and made one Commonwealth, and one Church; and each Tribe was subject to the Laws and Commands of the whole Society, and of the Chief Ru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ler or Rulers thereof; so its disobedience to their just com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mands was properly Rebellion against them.</ns0:note>
                  </ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="20">20 <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">Chap. 7. 1, 5.</ns0:note> Did not Achan the son of Zerah <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> One of his Posterity, <ns0:hi>Ios.</ns0:hi> 7. 17, 18.</ns0:note> com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mit a trespass in the accursed thing, and wrath fell on all the congregation of Israel, and that man perished not alone <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">But brought destruction upon his whole Family, and part of our Forces sent against <ns0:hi>Ai.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> in his iniquity <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>for his sin,</ns0:hi> of which see <ns0:hi>Ios.</ns0:hi> 7. 24.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="21">21 Then the children of Reuben, and the chil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dren of Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh, an<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />swered and said unto the heads of the thousands of Israel <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Either First properly, each was a Governour of a thou<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sand: for there were among them divers Rulers, some of Tens, some of Hundreds, and some of Thousands; or rather, Se<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />condly, improperly, and indefinitely, <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> of the People of <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> which consist of so many Thousands more than you, whose Authority therefore you owe a reverence to. For by comparing <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 14. these seem to be greater Persons than those that were Rulers of thousands.</ns0:note>,</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="22">22 The LORD God of gods <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">That <ns0:hi>Iehovah,</ns0:hi> whom we no less than you acknowledge and adore as the <ns0:hi>God of gods,</ns0:hi> infinitely superiour to all that are called Gods. The multiplying of his Titles, and the re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />petition of these words, shew their zeal and earnestness in this matter, and their abhorrency of the very thoughts of it.</ns0:note>, the Lord God of gods, he knoweth <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">To him we appeal who knoweth all things, and the truth of what we are now saying.</ns0:note>, and Israel he shall know, if <ns0:hi>it be</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Not onely our present words, but our future and constant course shall satisfie all <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> of our perseverance in the true Religion.</ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">If this have been done by us with such design, or in such a manner.</ns0:note>, in rebellion, or if in transgression against the LORD (save us not this day <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Thou, O Lord, to whom we have appealed, and without whom we cannot be saved or preserved, save us not from any of our Enemies, nor from the Sword of our Brethren. It is a sudden Apostrophe to God, usual in such vehement speeches.</ns0:note>).</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="23">23 That we have built us an altar to turn from following the LORD; or if to offer thereon burnt-offering, or meat-offering, or if to offer peace-offerings thereon, let the LORD himself re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />quire <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Call us to an account and punish us for it, as that Phrase is oft used, as <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 18. 19. 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 20. 16. <ns0:hi>Iob</ns0:hi> 10. 6. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 10. 13.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="24">24 And if we have not <ns0:hi>rather</ns0:hi> done it for fear of <ns0:hi>this</ns0:hi> thing, saying, <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> tomor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />row.</ns0:note> In time to come your chil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dren might speak unto our children, saying, What have ye to do with the LORD <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">You have no relation to him, nor interest in him, or his Worship.</ns0:note> God of Israel?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="25">25 For the LORD hath made Jordan a border between us and you <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">To shut you out of the Land of Promise, and conse<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />quently from the Covenant made between God and our fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers.</ns0:note>, ye children of Reuben, and Children of Gad, ye have no part in the LORD <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Nothing to do with him, no right to serve him or expect favour from him. See the like Phrase. 2 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 20. 1. <ns0:hi>Ezra</ns0:hi> 4. 8. <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 13. 3.</ns0:note>: so shall your children make our children cease from fearing the LORD.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="26">26 Therefore we said, Let us now prepare to build an altar, not for burnt-offering, nor for sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />crifice.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="27">27 But <ns0:hi>that it may be</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Gen. 31. 48. Chap. 24. 27. <ns0:hi>vers.</ns0:hi> 34.</ns0:note> a witness between us and you, and our generations after us, that we might do the service of the LORD before him <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">That we and ours may have and hold our Priviledge of serving and worshipping God; not upon this Altar, but in the place of Gods presence, in your Tabernacle, and upon your Altar.</ns0:note> with our burnt-offerings, and with our sacrifices, and with our peace-offerings, that your children may not say to our children in time to come, Ye have no part in the LORD.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="28">28 Therefore said we, That it shall be, when they should <ns0:hi>so</ns0:hi> say to us, or to our generations in time to come, that we may say <ns0:hi>again,</ns0:hi> Behold the pattern <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">An exact representation and resemblance.</ns0:note> of the Altar of the LORD, which our fathers made, not for burnt-offerings, nor for sacri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fices: but it <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> a witness between us and you <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">That we both serve one God, and approve and make use of one and the same Altar.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="29">29 God forbid that we should rebel against the LORD, and turn this day from following the LORD, to build an altar for burnt-offerings, for meat-offerings, or for sacrifices, besides the altar of the LORD our God that <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> before his taberna<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cle.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="30">30 And when Phinehas the priest, and the prin<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ces of the congregation, and heads of the thou<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sands of Israel which <ns0:hi>were</ns0:hi> with him, heard the words that the Children of Reuben, and the chil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dren of Gad, and the children of Manasseh spake, <ns0:note place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> it was <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> in their eyes.</ns0:note> it pleased them <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">They were fully satisfied with this answer.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="31">31 And Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest said unto the children of Reuben, and to the chil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dren of Gad, and to the children of Manasseh, This day we perceive that the LORD is among us <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">By his gracious presence, and preventing goodness, in keeping you from so great an offence, and all of us from those dismal calamities that would have followed upon it.</ns0:note>, because ye have not committed this trespass against the LORD: <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> then</ns0:note> now ye have delivered the children of Israel out of the hand of the LORD<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">i. e. From the Wrath and dreadful Judgments of God, by avoiding that Sin which would have involved both you and us in a most Bloody War; you have delivered us from the evils we feared. He that prevents an unexpected or ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />proaching Disease or Mischief, doth as truly deliver a man from it, as he that cures or removes it after it hath been in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />flicted.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="32">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:189" />32 ¶ And Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest, and the princes, returned from the children of Reuben, and from the children of Gad, out of the land of Gilead, unto the land of Canaan, to the children of Israel, and brought them word again.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="33">33 And the thing pleased the children of Is<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rael, and the children of Israel blessed God, and did not intend to go up against them in battel, to destroy the land <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">As they were by the Law of God obliged to do, if they had been guilty and persisted therein, as afterwards they did the Tribe of <ns0:hi>Benjamin</ns0:hi> for the same reason.</ns0:note> wherein the children of Reuben and Gad dwelt.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="34">34 And the children of Reuben and the children of Gad called the altar <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">That is, a Witness. So chap. 24. 27.</ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:hi>Ed,</ns0:hi> for it <ns0:hi>shall be</ns0:hi> a witness between us, that the LORD <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> God.</ns0:p>
